We have a task: extract SMILES string efficiently. We have mass spec data: m/z 276.066555... likely molecular ion [M+H]+? The mass 276.0666 suggests formula maybe C15H12ClO3? Let's compute: C15H12ClO3 exact mass: C15=15*12.0000=180, H12=12*1.007825=12.0939, Cl=34.9689, O3=3*15.9949=47.9847 total = 180+12.0939+34.9689+47.9847=274. (calc) 180+12.0939=192.0939; +34.9689=227.0628; +47.9847=275.0475. That's 275.0475. Not 276.0666. Maybe [M+Na]+? Add 22.9898 gives 298.0373. Not match. Maybe [M+H]+ of C15H13ClO3? C15H13ClO3 mass: add 1.0078 => 276.0553. Slight off 276.0666 difference 0.0113. Could be C15H13ClO3? Let's compute exact: C15 180, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847 sum = 275. (180+13.1017=193.1017; +34.9689=228.0706; +47.9847=276.0553). Observed 276.0666, diff 0.0113 maybe due to measurement error. So formula likely C15H13ClO3. DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 = 15 -13/2 +1 =15 -6.5 +1 =9.5? Wait halogen counts as H. For formula with halogen, treat Cl as H. So effective H =13+1=14. DBE = C - (H+X)/2 + N/2 +1 =15 -14/2 +1 =15 -7 +1 =9. So DBE 9. That suggests aromatic rings etc.

We have carbon NMR peaks: many aromatic carbons (166,151,144,140,137,131,131,124,122,119,116,116) plus aliphatic 61.10, 14.26. So likely a phenoxy ethyl group (O-CH2-CH3) gives 61 (O-CH2) and 14 (CH3). Also carbonyl carbon at 166. So structure maybe a phenyl ester with chloro substituent.

We have chlorine present. Possibly 4-chlorophenoxyacetophenone? Let's think: Clc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)OCH2CH3? That would be 4-chlorobenzoyl ethyl ester. Formula: C9H5ClO (benzoyl) + C2H5O (ethyl) = C11H10ClO2? Wait compute: C9H5ClO (C7? Actually benzoyl: C7H5ClO? Let's compute: 4-chlorobenzoyl: C7H4ClO? Actually benzoyl group C6H4Cl-CO- = C7H4ClO. Add ethoxy OCH2CH3: OCH2CH3 adds C2H5O. Total C9H9ClO2? Not match.

Our carbon NMR shows carbonyl at 166, aromatic many, O-CH2 at 61, CH3 at 14. So likely an ester of aromatic acid with ethyl group. Also chlorine on aromatic ring.

Formula C15H13ClO3 matches: aromatic acid C8H5ClO2? plus ethyl (C2H5O) plus phenyl? Let's compute: Ethyl ester of 4-chlorosalicylic acid? That would have extra OH.

But we have OCH2CH3 (61,14) and carbonyl (166). Also maybe phenoxy group (Ar-O-). The carbon at 61 could be O-CH2 attached to aromatic O (phenoxy). So maybe ethoxy attached to phenoxy? Actually O-CH2-CH3 is ethoxy attached to carbonyl (ester). So carbonyl carbon 166, O-CH2 61, CH3 14.

Thus structure: ethyl 4-chlorobenzoate? That formula C9H7ClO2? Wait ethyl benzoate C9H10O2? Actually benzoic acid C7H6O2, plus ethyl adds C2H5 => C9H11O2? Let's compute: C7H6O2 + C2H5 = C9H11O2. Add Cl gives C9H10ClO2? Not match.

Our formula C15H13ClO3 suggests two aromatic rings (C12) plus ethoxy (C2) plus carbonyl carbon (1) =15. So likely a phenyl ester of chlorobenzoic acid: e.g., 4-chlorobenzoyl phenyl ether? Wait phenyl ester would have two phenyl rings: one from acid, one from alcohol. So acid: C7H4ClO (benzoyl with Cl) plus phenol O-CH2? Actually phenyl alcohol is phenol (C6H5OH) gives O-CH? Not ethoxy.

But we have ethoxy not phenoxy. So maybe acid is chlorophenyl, alcohol is phenol? That would give O-CH (no ethyl). Not match.

Alternative: 4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid ethyl ester? That would have aromatic ring (C6H4ClO), CH2 (O-CH2) at 61, carbonyl 166, ethyl group attached to carbonyl (CH3 14, CH2 maybe 30 not seen). But we have only one aliphatic carbon at 61 and 14, missing CH2 of ethyl attached to carbonyl (should be around 30). So maybe the ethyl is attached to oxygen of phenoxy, not carbonyl. So structure: phenoxy ethyl (O-CH2-CH3) attached to aromatic carbonyl? Actually that's ethoxy phenyl ether: phenoxy ethyl? Wait.

Consider compound: 4-chlorobenzoyl ethyl ether? Not.

Maybe it's 4-chlorophenoxyacetophenone? That would have carbonyl attached to phenyl, and O-CH2-CH3 attached to other phenyl. That gives two aromatic rings, carbonyl, O-CH2 (61), CH3 (14). Formula: C15H13ClO2? plus extra O? Actually O-CH2-CH3 adds O and two carbons, plus carbonyl O. So total O3. Yes matches C15H13ClO3.

Structure: 4-chlorophenoxyacetophenone? Let's draw: phenyl-CO-CH2-O-PhCl? Wait carbonyl attached to phenyl (acetophenone) gives C6H5-CO-CH2-? Actually acetophenone is Ph-CO-CH3. Here we have Ph-CO-CH2-O-PhCl? That would have carbonyl carbon (166), CH2 attached to carbonyl (should be ~30) not observed. So not.

Our aliphatic carbon at 61 suggests O-CH2 attached to O (ether). So CH2 attached to O and aromatic ring maybe. So O-CH2-PhCl. The carbonyl carbon attached to aromatic ring (phenyl) and O (ester). So structure: phenyl carbonyl (benzoyl) attached to O-CH2-PhCl (aryl ether). That's phenyl benzoate with chloro phenyl substituent on the alcohol side. So it's 4-chlorophenyl benzoate? That would be C13H9ClO2? Actually benzoic acid (C7H6O2) + phenol (C6H5OH) gives C13H10O3? Wait benzoic acid + phenol forms benzoate ester: C7H5O2 + C6H5O = C13H10O3. Add Cl gives C13H9ClO3. Not C15.

Our formula C15 suggests extra two carbons, maybe ethoxy group attached to phenyl ring (para-ethoxy). So maybe 4-ethoxy-3-chlorobenzaldehyde? But carbonyl at 166 suggests aldehyde? Aldehyde carbonyl ~190-200. So 166 is ester.

Thus maybe ethyl 4-chlorophenyl carbonate? Not.

Let's compute formula for ethyl 4-chlorophenyl carbonate: O=C(OCH2CH3)O-PhCl. Atoms: carbonyl C (1), ethoxy C2, phenyl C6, plus carbonyl carbon? Already counted. Total C = 1+2+6 =9? plus maybe extra carbon? Not 15.

We need two phenyl rings (12 C) + carbonyl carbon (1) + ethoxy carbon (2) =15. So structure: diphenyl carbonate with ethoxy? Actually diphenyl carbonate is O=C(OPh)OPh (C13). Add ethoxy would be O=C(OPh)OCH2CH3 gives C13? Wait carbonyl C (1) + phenyl (6) + ethoxy (2) =9? plus second phenyl (6) =15. Yes O=C(OPh)OCH2CH3 gives C15. Add Cl on phenyl gives C15H13ClO3. So compound is ethyl phenyl carbonate with chloro substituent on phenyl ring. That matches carbonyl 166, O-CH2 61, CH3 14, aromatic carbons many.

Thus SMILES: Clc1ccc(cc1)OC(=O)OCC. Let's validate: Clc1ccc(cc1)OC(=O)OCC. Use validate: earlier we validated "Clc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Oc2ccc(cc2)OCC" which is different (chlorophenyl carbonyl attached to phenoxy ethyl). Our candidate: Clc1ccc(cc1)OC(=O)OCC (chloro phenyl carbonate ethyl). Let's validate.
